material_use: Supports statements about sanitary employee toilet facilities; dry walking surfaces; sanitary waste removal; and employee-health boundaries.
limitations: Applies to covered permanent places of employment and employees. It does not determine customer access duties, local plumbing code, accessibility obligations, vendor scope or a site-specific cleanup method.

material_use: Supports the operator need to preserve prompt employee access to sanitary toilet facilities and functioning handwashing provisions.
limitations: Overview is not a substitute for the regulation or legal advice. It does not establish a universal alternate-restroom plan for every facility.

publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
provenance: Authoritative federal public-health guidance; page dated 2026-06-11
material_use: Supports the warning not to mix household cleaners, including ammonia with chlorine bleach.
limitations: Chemical-emergency guidance; not a sewage-remediation procedure or commercial-facility work instruction.

material_use: Supports a conservative boundary around potentially sewage- or chemical-contaminated water and the use of qualified professionals when cleanup may be unsafe or difficult.
limitations: Written for flooded homes, not a self-storage restroom. Used only for general contamination and qualified-help boundaries, not for a prescriptive cleanup recipe.

material_use: Supports avoiding contact with sewage backup and consulting appropriate health or regulatory authorities for guidance.
limitations: Primarily addresses residential or onsite septic systems. It does not establish the source of a commercial restroom backup or define a facility-specific remediation scope.
